why_how.text: At a railroad crossing, drivers should listen and look in both directions for trains and their warning signals.
Do not proceed through a railroad crossing until certain that doing so is safe.
When a railroad stop is required, the handbook says the driver should stop at least fifteen feet and no more than fifty feet from the nearest rail.
Active flashing railroad warning lights require a stop, and further movement is allowed only when safe.
Never drive through, beneath or around a railroad gate that is down or being lowered.
Never stop while any part of the vehicle is on railroad tracks.
In traffic, do not enter a railroad crossing unless there is enough room beyond it for the vehicle's full length.
Do not ignore a railroad warning signal or drive around lowered gates even when no approaching train is visible.
Do not change gears while crossing railroad tracks because doing so may stall the vehicle there.
Never try to beat a train to a crossing.
Before proceeding over multiple railroad tracks, make sure another train is not approaching on a different track.
Watch for buses and trucks that are required to stop at railroad crossings, since some must stop at every crossing.
Look in both directions when approaching railroad tracks even if the flashing warning signal is not working.

why_how.text: A thru-turn intersection manages traffic by prohibiting direct left turns.
For a left turn at a thru-turn intersection, first continue through, use the marked U-turn at the next signal downstream, return toward the intersection and turn right.
A single point urban interchange controls turns from a single signal-controlled point at the interchange center.
At the described single point urban interchange, stop at the stop lines so the vehicle does not extend into cross-traffic.
To go straight through the described single point urban interchange, stay in either of its two through lanes.
To turn left onto the highway at the described single point urban interchange, use the lanes marked for left turns.
The single point urban interchange's exit ramp separates traffic into left-turn and right-turn lanes.

After mistakenly exiting at the described single point urban interchange, do not cross straight to reenter; turn left or right onto the intersecting highway and find a safe turnaround to the correct freeway entrance.
For a right turn after exiting the interstate at the described single point urban interchange, remain in the right lane, yield, turn right, merge and watch for pedestrians.
For a left turn after exiting the interstate at the single point urban interchange, use the left exit lane, merge onto the highway and watch for pedestrians.
The described single point urban interchange provides crosswalks, bicycle paths and pedestrian signals.
Pedestrians and bicyclists at the described single point urban interchange use the signalized crossing and are directed to the central pedestrian island.
